name: amit-mizrachi
description: Amit Mizrachi's Claude Code skills. next-prompt hands work off to a fresh background agent; night-sprint delivers a whole feature overnight as one PR (one per repo when the feature spans several repos), with async reviews that each run one deep-review reviewer (or a roster of Claude and Codex reviewers named in one AGENTS.md line) and an optional blitz mode that runs tickets side by side on their dependency graph, and ends with an async retro that opens draft PRs for the environment fixes it finds, or runs research in research mode; product-research takes one approval and returns a cited research artifact built from your connectors and the web; night-marathon takes a feature from research to a plan artifact with realistic UI mockups and a decision pick list to one PR, autonomously or with your picks in between; agent-fix takes one reported AI agent issue from eval cases proved RED, through a fix weighed with Codex and Fable, to a PR proved GREEN, a before/after summary artifact and a Slack approval request, with the diagnose/reproduce/prove know-how supplied by role skills a domain repo declares in one AGENTS.md line; to-spec and to-tickets turn a feature into a spec and tracer-bullet tickets, callable by agents as well as humans; deep-review reviews a diff with one Opus reviewer at high effort instead of a squad; mywayfinder draws a wayfinder map's blocking graph as a published chart. fable-review runs deep-review with one Fable subagent, then verifies and fixes its findings; address-review fixes and replies to every review comment on a PR (Fixed in <sha> / Skipped: <reason>, with reasoning). wait-what (re-pitch the last message plainly) and retro (a session retrospective that proposes environment fixes) are slash commands copied from mattpocock/skills, with writing-for-agents, the style guide retro loads. Ships codex-bridge, an MCP server that lets Claude ask OpenAI Codex questions, which night-marathon uses for a second opinion on the plan when it is connected. Ships night-watch, a terminal command that draws a live progress board of every sprint and marathon on the machine, linked onto your PATH by a SessionStart hook. Ships a macOS caffeinate hook that keeps the machine awake for a sliding 8 hours after the last Claude interaction.
